passages.title: 3D Printing
passages.text: I primarily use resin 3D printing to make tabletop models.

passages.title: 3D Printing
passages.text: I work with an Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K and Lychee Slicer, handling preparation, printing, cleaning, curing, and assembly myself. The models I currently print come from STL files created by other designers.

passages.title: 3D Printing
passages.text: I’ve fine-tuned printer settings to produce accurate prints with fine detail. I’ve also worked on model orientation and support placement to reduce printing failures and avoid problems with hollow pieces.

passages.title: 3D Printing
passages.text: My next goal is to learn how to create some of my own models in Blender. I’m considering simple objects, such as dice, as a starting point before developing more involved mechanical and character ideas.

passages.title: About Me
passages.text: I’m Matthew Gravina, and I’m pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Cybersecurity at Brigham Young University–Idaho after previously attending Modesto Junior College. My interests include computer systems, resin 3D printing, miniatures, and understanding how things work.

passages.title: About Me
passages.text: I’m a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and an Eagle Scout. I served a mission in Tucson, Arizona, which ended early because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

passages.title: About Me
passages.text: Outside coursework, I enjoy hands-on projects and spending time with my pets. Some of their less dignified moments may also find their way into this portfolio.

passages.title: About Me
passages.text: My current coursework includes networking, web development, electronics, and artificial intelligence. I’m practicing network configuration and troubleshooting, building websites with HTML and CSS, and working with circuits and wireless controllers.

passages.title: About Me
passages.text: Alongside my classes, I’m learning about 3D modeling in Blender so I can begin creating my own printable designs.

passages.title: About Me
passages.text: Outside class, I enjoy stories and imaginative worlds. I grew up with Pokémon, Spider-Man, and little green toy soldiers. That childhood interest in miniature armies is part of what draws me to Warhammer today, alongside its stories and theme.

passages.title: About Me
passages.text: I’ve also enjoyed playing Dungeons & Dragons and writing stories of my own, although I haven’t spent as much time on those interests lately.

passages.title: About Me
passages.text: Finding Nemo was a childhood favorite, and my fascination with the ocean has stayed with me. Space captures my imagination too—another great ocean to explore.

passages.title: ECEN / Tank Project
passages.text: I’m applying electronics coursework to practical circuits and a personal model tank project.

passages.title: ECEN / Tank Project
passages.text: I’m working toward a wirelessly controlled model tank using a freely available model that resembles a Warhammer 40,000 Baneblade.

passages.title: ECEN / Tank Project
passages.text: So far, I’ve established a wireless connection between my controller badge and an ESP32 receiver. Inputs from the badge appear on a display connected to the receiver. I’m currently printing parts and ordering the other components needed for assembly.

passages.title: ECEN / Tank Project
passages.text: The next goal is to assemble the tank and use the wireless controls to drive it. Physical movement remains a work in progress.

passages.title: ECEN / Tank Project
passages.text: Model credit: Broadsword Superheavy Tank by nfeyma, available on Cults3D.

passages.title: ECEN / Tank Project
passages.text: In a classroom circuit, I checked the connections, repaired a loose motor lead by soldering it, and tested the motor separately. The circuit worked after I reversed the transistor’s orientation.

passages.title: ECEN / Tank Project
passages.text: My teacher explained that the supplied transistor had a different lead order. The exercise gave me practice checking individual parts and connections when a circuit did not work as expected.

passages.title: Personal Portfolio
passages.text: I’m Matthew Gravina, a cybersecurity student at Brigham Young University–Idaho. I’m interested in understanding computer systems and finding tools and methods that help people and make those systems more secure. This portfolio brings together my coursework, personal projects, and interests.

passages.title: Personal Portfolio
passages.text: Explore my work in web development, networking, electronics, resin 3D printing, and marine biology coursework. I use these pages to share what I’ve tried, what I’ve learned, and what I’m still developing.

passages.title: Personal Portfolio
passages.text: I’m studying cybersecurity while building a foundation in networking, web development, electronics, and artificial intelligence. Through coursework and personal projects, I’m practicing how to follow a process, test results, and investigate problems when something doesn’t work as expected.

passages.title: Marine Biology
passages.text: I took a marine biology course at Modesto Junior College and enjoyed the hands-on work.

passages.title: Marine Biology
passages.text: I particularly enjoyed the dissections. I practiced careful handling and removing parts cleanly while examining their structure.

passages.title: Marine Biology
passages.text: My course photos include specimens before and after dissection. I’m developing this collection with descriptions of the work I completed.

passages.title: Networking Skills
passages.text: I’m studying networking as part of my cybersecurity degree at BYU–Idaho.

passages.title: Networking Skills
passages.text: I use Cisco Packet Tracer and command-line tools for guided academic labs. My practice includes IP addressing, subnetting, VLANs, and testing connectivity with ping.

passages.title: Networking Skills
passages.text: I have worked on switch configurations and link aggregation. I’m continuing to develop these skills and document individual labs.

passages.title: Web Development
passages.text: I’m learning web development through Web Fundamentals at BYU–Idaho. These projects help me practice HTML structure, CSS layout, and working with links, images, tables, and forms. I use course guidance and AI assistance as I learn.

passages.title: Web Development
passages.text: Full webpage assembly, my first introduction to HTML and CSS. I learned how HTML organizes a website’s content and how CSS controls its appearance. This project helped me practice connecting pages, images, and styles into a complete website.

passages.title: Web Development
passages.text: I learned how to use CSS to arrange text, images, and lists within a card. I also practiced adjusting spacing, alignment, and typography to match a reference design.

passages.title: Web Development
passages.text: I learned how to organize information into an HTML table using rows, headings, and data cells. I also practiced creating form fields and connecting labels to their inputs.

passages.title: Web Development
passages.text: I learned how to give an existing HTML page a holiday theme using only CSS. I practiced changing colors, typography, spacing, and image shapes without modifying the HTML.

passages.title: Web Development
passages.text: I learned how to arrange elements to match different reference layouts. This exercise helped me understand how parent containers, CSS Grid, and positioning rules affect where elements appear.

passages.title: Web Development
passages.text: I learned how to recreate flag designs by placing colored elements within a CSS Grid. I practiced controlling grid rows, columns, spacing, and overlapping elements to form each design.

passages.title: Web Development
passages.text: An image gallery arranged with CSS Grid. Smaller preview images link to larger JPEG versions, and a hover effect changes the image opacity. The exercise explores image dimensions, file formats, and file size.

passages.title: Web Development
passages.text: I practiced styling a signup form with HTML and CSS, using CSS Grid, spacing, and typography to match a reference design. I also explored how JavaScript responds to a form submission and handles the information entered by the user.
